code.originalText: Eighteen-week review: grief, no smoking, urate toward target and his writing

text.paragraph: Eighteen-week review: grief, no smoking, urate toward target and his writing. [S]

Mr. Clemens returns three weeks after his wellness visit, a few days before he leaves for his winter home. He has had fifteen grief therapy sessions and will finish the sixteenth next week. He visits the places he used to avoid, has given some of his wife's things to people who will use them, and is finishing a long essay. He dines with friends every week. He sleeps about six hours. He has smoked no cigars for eight weeks and has finished twelve weeks of varenicline. He has had no gout since August and no chest tightness. His stool test and hepatitis C antibody were negative, and the ultrasound showed a normal aorta. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-16; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 128/76, pulse 70; weight 65.4 kg, BMI 21.9
Warm and witty; speaks of his wife in the past tense with affection
Persistent yearning for his wife, broken sleep, low mood and withdrawal from friends and work, a year after her death; cause under evaluation
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to his wife's documented death a year before; resolved into the diagnosis of prolonged grief disorder at the consultation. Not a claim about his real grief.

Prolonged grief disorder (DSM-5-TR): more than 12 months after his wife's death, daily yearning and preoccupation with her, with intense emotional pain, a sense that part of himself has died, avoidance of reminders, loneliness, difficulty taking up his work and life again, and a feeling that life is meaningless; PG-13-R 41; major depression not present
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the consultation, anchored to his documented bereavements. Not a claim about his real mental health; the roster's bipolar lead is not used.
Tobacco use disorder, cigars: about fifteen cigars a day, smoking since boyhood, some smoke inhaled; first cigar within thirty minutes of waking
S — Synthetic modern coding anchored to his documented smoking since boyhood.
Chest tightness on climbing steep hills, twice in the past month, easing within five minutes of rest; none at rest; cause under evaluation
S — Synthetic presenting symptom; resolved into a diagnosis at five weeks after CT coronary angiography. Not a claim about his real heart in 1905; his documented chest pain began in 1909.

Coronary artery disease, nonobstructive (CAD-RADS 2: 25 to 49 percent narrowing of the proximal left anterior descending artery; coronary calcium score 410), with exertional chest tightness that has not recurred on treatment; treated with a statin, aspirin and stopping smoking
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at five weeks. Not a claim about his real coronary arteries.
Gout, recurrent flares of the big toe since his late fifties, two in the past year; serum urate 8.6 mg/dL; no tophi
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to his documented gout.
Acute bronchitis, likely viral, for six days in a cigar smoker; no pneumonia on examination; resolved within three weeks without antibiotics
S — Synthetic acute illness; not a historical claim; his documented bronchitis was in later years.
